# Characteristic Functions

The **characteristic function** `χ_A(x)` of a set `A` over a universe `U` returns 1 when `x ∈ A` and
0 otherwise. It is the bridge between set algebra and ordinary arithmetic: every set operation
becomes a pointwise numeric operation on 0/1 vectors.

The four identities lab 3 of [[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] implements and checks:

```
χ_(A∩B)(x) = min(χ_A(x), χ_B(x))
χ_(A∪B)(x) = max(χ_A(x), χ_B(x))
χ_(A′)(x)  = 1 − χ_A(x)
|A|        = Σ_{x∈U} χ_A(x)
```

The last one is the payoff: **cardinality is a sum**. Once a set is a vector of indicators, counting,
intersecting and complementing are all arithmetic, which is why bitsets, Bloom filters and columnar
database predicates all work the way they do.

## What the lab builds around it

- `Set`, `MultiSet` and `EmptySet` implemented **from scratch over native lists**, not Python's
  builtin `set` — the exercise is owning the operations, not calling them.
- **Power set** and **Cartesian product** constructors.
- **Inclusion–exclusion**: `|A∪B| = |A| + |B| − |A∩B|`, verifiable against the χ-sum definition
  above, which is the cleanest way to see why the correction term exists.
- A **propositional parser** producing truth tables — the logical twin of the same machinery, since a
  truth table *is* a characteristic function over assignments.

## The only automated check in the repo

`lab3_Sets/mandatory_tasks/test_suite.py` is a hand-rolled `TestRunner`: boolean assertions, ✓/✗
output, a pass/fail summary returning a bool. Not [[pytest]] — this repo has no test framework and no
CI. It is nevertheless the only place in
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] where a claim is machine-checked rather than screenshotted.

A related commit records what running it on Windows cost:
`48ba16d Fix UnicodeEncodeError in the lab3 demos on Windows consoles` — the `∈ ∪ χ Σ` glyphs printed
in the demos are not safe on a cp1252 console. See
[[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]].
